home.intro: Rivers, Tourism, Resource Reliance and Atmospheric Hazards have interactive revision notes with Active Recall questions. Write your answer first, then use Compare with model to see the model answer.

hydrograph.title: Storm Hydrograph
hydrograph.description: An illustrative model of how a catchment responds to rain, not a forecast for any real river. The sliders set relative scenario conditions, not measured percentages. Compare the peak of rainfall intensity with the peak of discharge: the time between them is the lag time.
hydrograph.subduedNote: In this scenario the response is slower and more spread out: lag time is longer and the peak comes later. Real hydrographs also depend on basin size, slope, soil type and storm duration.
hydrograph.flashyNote: In this scenario the water reaches the river sooner: lag time is shorter and the discharge peak is high. This illustrates a tendency, not a prediction for a real catchment.

circulation.title: Atmospheric Circulation
circulation.description: Explore a simplified model of average atmospheric circulation that ignores differences between longitudes. Pressure belts and boundaries migrate; continents, oceans and seasons create regional differences.
circulation.hoverHint: Hover over or tap a cell to see its description.
circulation.legendLow: L = relatively low pressure; rising air often produces clouds and rain
circulation.legendHigh: H = relatively high pressure; sinking air often keeps clouds from forming
circulation.summary: Approximate pattern: tropical ascent, subtropical descent, subpolar ascent and polar descent. This helps explain climate belts but is not a weather forecast.

hadleyN.name: Hadley (N)
hadleyN.desc: Northern Hadley cell: air rises near the equator, moves north aloft and sinks in the northern subtropics. Near the surface, north-east trade winds carry the air back towards the equator.

ferrelN.name: Ferrel (N)
ferrelN.desc: Northern Ferrel cell: near the surface, air moves towards the pole and westerly winds blow from the south-west. Aloft, air returns towards the equator. Mid-latitude weather systems, not direct heating, keep this cell going.

polarN.name: Polar (N)
polarN.desc: Northern polar cell: cold, dense air sinks near the North Pole, moves south near the surface and rises at subpolar latitudes. The polar easterlies there blow from the north-east.

polarS.name: Polar (S)
polarS.desc: Southern polar cell: cold air sinks over Antarctica, flows north near the surface and climbs again at subpolar latitudes. Near the ground, these polar easterlies blow from the south-east.

ferrelS.name: Ferrel (S)
ferrelS.desc: Southern Ferrel cell: surface westerlies come from the north-west and push air towards the pole. Air returns towards the equator higher up. Passing mid-latitude storms drive this indirect cell, not direct heating.

hadleyS.name: Hadley (S)
hadleyS.desc: Southern Hadley cell: warm air rises close to the equator, flows south high up and descends across the southern subtropics. The south-east trade winds near the ground return it to the equator.

fieldwork.title: Fieldwork & Research
fieldwork.intro: Geographers collect data during fieldwork and then interpret it. The terms in this section help you plan an investigation and explain its results in longer exam answers.

aim.name: Aim
aim.rule: An aim is the question that the investigation is designed to answer. It states what will be studied and where.
examples: Aim: investigate how channel width changes along a selected river reach.

contrast.en: An aim says what to investigate; a hypothesis is a testable prediction that the data can support or reject.
contrast.ru: Цель показывает, что именно изучать; гипотеза (hypothesis) — проверяемое предположение, которое данные могут подтвердить или опровергнуть.

hypothesis.name: Hypothesis
hypothesis.rule: A hypothesis is a testable statement about an expected relationship or difference between measurable variables. It must be possible to show that it is false, so that data can reject it. Plan the measurements in advance, so that the evidence can test it fairly.
examples: Alternative hypothesis (H₁): mean channel width increases with distance downstream along this reach.

contrast.en: Evidence can support a hypothesis for the sample studied, but it does not prove a general rule.
contrast.ru: Данные могут подтвердить гипотезу для изученной выборки, но не доказывают общего правила.

nullHypothesis.name: Null hypothesis (H₀)
nullHypothesis.rule: The null hypothesis (H₀) is the statement that a test checks. In a simple fieldwork test, it usually says that there is no difference or association between the variables in the population being studied. The alternative hypothesis contradicts it and describes the expected effect.
examples: H₀: there is no association between distance downstream and channel width in the population being studied.

contrast.en: Failing to reject H₀ does not prove that no relationship exists: the sample may be too small or the measurements too variable.
contrast.ru: Если H₀ не удалось отвергнуть, это ещё не доказывает отсутствия связи: выборка может быть слишком мала или измерения слишком разбросаны.

primary.name: Primary data
primary.rule: Evidence collected first-hand for the present investigation, using an explicit method such as measurement, observation or an interview.
examples: Your river-depth measurements and your recorded interview responses are both primary data.

contrast.en: Primary and secondary describe where the data came from; quantitative and qualitative describe the kind of information.
contrast.ru: Первичные и вторичные данные различаются по происхождению, а количественные и качественные — по характеру информации.

sources.title: Harrison & Torres — Geography for the IB MYP 4&5: by Concept (Hodder, 2019)
sources.section: ch. 1 'What do geographers do?', pp. 2–27 — section not identified; text not checked (book not on Mac)

secondary.name: Secondary data
secondary.rule: Existing evidence reused for an investigation, originally collected by someone else or for another purpose. Check its date, scale, definitions and collection method.
examples: A published rainfall series used to interpret your river measurements is secondary data.

contrast.en: Secondary data are not necessarily unreliable: official statistics may cover more places and years than a survey by one class.
contrast.ru: Вторичные данные не обязательно ненадёжны: официальная статистика может охватывать больше мест и лет, чем опрос одного класса.

sources.title: Harrison & Torres — Geography for the IB MYP 4&5: by Concept (Hodder, 2019)
sources.section: ch. 1 'What do geographers do?', pp. 2–27 — section not identified; text not checked (book not on Mac)

quantitative.name: Quantitative data
quantitative.rule: Numerical results of counting or measuring, which can be compared directly. Counts give whole numbers; measurements, such as depth, can take any value in a range but are recorded to a set precision.
examples: The number of cars passing a junction in an hour is a count; the speed of a river's current is a measurement.

contrast.en: A number used only as a label, such as a land-use code, is not a measured quantity.
contrast.ru: Число, которое служит лишь названием категории (например, кодом типа землепользования), — не измеренная величина.

sources.title: Harrison & Torres — Geography for the IB MYP 4&5: by Concept (Hodder, 2019)
sources.section: ch. 1 'What do geographers do?', pp. 2–27 — section not identified; text not checked (book not on Mac)

qualitative.name: Qualitative data
qualitative.rule: Descriptions, categories or opinions that express qualities, meanings or experiences, such as a land-use type or what residents say in an interview. They can be coded and compared using consistent rules.
examples: Recording a site as residential, retail or park gives qualitative data. A resident's comment on why they use the park adds an explanation.

contrast.en: Qualitative does not automatically mean subjective or poor quality: a land-use type can be recorded by direct observation.
contrast.ru: Качественные данные не обязательно субъективны или плохи: тип землепользования можно записать прямым наблюдением.

sources.title: Harrison & Torres — Geography for the IB MYP 4&5: by Concept (Hodder, 2019)

sampleSize.name: Sample size
sampleSize.rule: The number of observational units included in a sample, written n. State whether a unit is a person, site, pebble or independent measurement.
examples: If the investigation compares sites, many pebbles from one site still represent only one sampled site. If the population of interest is the pebbles at that site, the pebbles are the sampling units; independence depends on how they are selected.

contrast.en: A larger sample can reduce random sampling error; it cannot automatically remove selection bias.
contrast.ru: Большая выборка может уменьшить случайную ошибку, но сама по себе не устраняет смещение отбора (selection bias).

sources.title: Harrison & Torres — Geography for the IB MYP 4&5: by Concept (Hodder, 2019)
sources.section: ch. 1 'What do geographers do?', pp. 2–27 — section not identified; text not checked (book not on Mac)

systematic.name: Systematic sampling
systematic.rule: Observations are taken at a fixed step (every N-th one) along a route, from an ordered list or over time. Ideally, the first observation is chosen at random.
examples: Start at a randomly chosen point along the route, then record the land use at equal intervals decided before fieldwork begins.

contrast.en: Regular spacing is efficient, but it can coincide with a repeating pattern in the landscape, such as evenly spaced houses, and bias the sample.
contrast.ru: Равные интервалы удобны, но могут совпасть с повторяющимся узором местности, например с равномерно расставленными домами, и исказить выборку.

sources.title: Harrison & Torres — Geography for the IB MYP 4&5: by Concept (Hodder, 2019)
sources.section: ch. 1 'What do geographers do?', pp. 2–27 — section not identified; text not checked (book not on Mac)

stratified.name: Stratified sampling
stratified.rule: Stratified sampling divides the population into non-overlapping groups that matter for the question, and takes observations within every group. In proportional stratified sampling, each group supplies a share of the sample equal to its share of the population.
examples: If most of a study area is residential and only a small part is parkland, a proportional sample takes most of its sites in the residential zone.

contrast.en: Stratified sampling makes sure every group is represented; a simple random sample may, by chance, miss a small group.
contrast.ru: Стратифицированная выборка обеспечивает представленность каждой группы, а простая случайная выборка может по воле случая не включить небольшую группу.

sources.title: Harrison & Torres — Geography for the IB MYP 4&5: by Concept (Hodder, 2019)
sources.section: ch. 1 'What do geographers do?', pp. 2–27 — section not identified; text not checked (book not on Mac)

random.name: Simple random sampling
random.rule: In a simple random sample of n distinct units from a defined population, every possible set of n units has the same probability of selection. Each individual unit therefore also has the same inclusion probability.
examples: Number all eligible sites and use a random-number generator to select them.

contrast.en: Choosing whoever is easiest to reach is convenience sampling, not random sampling, even if the choice looks haphazard.
contrast.ru: Выбор тех, до кого легче всего добраться, — удобная выборка (convenience sampling), а не случайная, даже если выбор кажется бессистемным.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.body: A methodology explains what is measured or observed, where, when and how, so that someone else could repeat the work. Reduce errors by repeating measurements and using the same equipment and method at every observation point. Follow the safety rules for every site you visit. Explain how each choice affects the question you are answering.

bar.name: Bar chart
bar.rule: Each bar shows a count or value for one category, so the bars compare categories with each other. Label each category, the quantity measured and its units, and normally start the value axis at zero so that bar lengths can be compared fairly.
examples: Compare pedestrian counts at several sites during equal time intervals.

contrast.en: A histogram groups numerical data into intervals, so its bars do not mean the same as category bars.
contrast.ru: Гистограмма (histogram) группирует числовые данные по интервалам, поэтому её столбцы означают другое, чем столбцы категорий.

line.name: Line graph
line.rule: Plot values in a meaningful sequence, usually against time or distance, and join adjacent observations to show change.
examples: Plot river discharge in m³/s against time in hours.

contrast.en: Do not join points for unordered categories, such as different sites: the line would suggest values between them that were never measured.
contrast.ru: Не соединяй точки линией для категорий без естественного порядка, например разных участков: линия подскажет значения между ними, которых не измеряли.

scatter.name: Scatter graph
scatter.rule: Each point shows a paired observation of two quantitative variables. The pattern helps identify direction, strength, outliers and possible non-linear relationships.
examples: Plot each site's measured channel width (vertical axis) against its distance downstream (horizontal axis).

contrast.en: Correlation does not prove causation: a third variable or the sampling method may explain the association.
contrast.ru: Корреляция не доказывает причинность: связь может объясняться третьей переменной или способом формирования выборки.

pie.name: Pie chart
pie.rule: Each sector shows one category's share of a single total, and the categories must not overlap. Sector angle = (category value ÷ total) × 360°.
examples: If a quarter of all survey answers fall into one category, its sector is 90°.

contrast.en: Use a bar chart if respondents can choose multiple overlapping categories; those shares need not sum to 100%.
contrast.ru: Если можно выбрать несколько пересекающихся категорий, используй столбчатую диаграмму: такие доли не обязаны давать 100%.

gis.name: Geographic information system (GIS)
gis.rule: A GIS is a computer system for storing, analysing and displaying data tied to geographic locations. Such data are often organised as map layers, one layer for each kind of data.
examples: Overlay building locations, ground elevation and a flood-extent layer to find buildings that may be at risk.

contrast.en: A GIS stores and analyses map data; a GPS receiver determines coordinates, which can then be entered into a GIS.
contrast.ru: ГИС хранит и анализирует картографические данные; приёмник GPS определяет координаты, которые затем можно внести в ГИС.

analysis.title: Data analysis
analysis.body: Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient (ρ) measures the direction and strength of a tendency for larger values of one variable to accompany larger or smaller values of another, using ranks. The relationship need not be a straight line. For at least two pairs with no tied ranks, ρ = 1 − (6Σd²) ÷ [n(n² − 1)], where d is each pair’s rank difference and n is the number of pairs. When defined, the value is between −1 and +1. A sample value of zero does not prove that the population variables are unrelated. To assess evidence against a stated null hypothesis, use an appropriate significance test or critical value for the sample size and alternative; simply comparing the coefficient with zero is insufficient. With ties, calculate correlation between average ranks; if either variable is constant, the coefficient is undefined.

contrast.en: Strength and significance are different questions: a strong coefficient from a small sample may not be statistically significant.
contrast.ru: Сила связи и её статистическая значимость — разные вопросы: сильный коэффициент на малой выборке может оказаться статистически незначимым.

conclusion.name: Conclusion
conclusion.rule: An evidence-based answer to the investigation aim. Refer to measured patterns, key values and exceptions, and state how far the hypothesis is supported.
examples: If width rose at most sites but not at the bridge site, the conclusion should say the hypothesis is only partly supported.

contrast.en: A conclusion answers the question; an evaluation assesses the evidence and method behind that answer.
contrast.ru: Вывод отвечает на вопрос исследования; оценка разбирает данные и методы, на которых основан этот ответ.

sources.title: Harrison & Torres — Geography for the IB MYP 4&5: by Concept (Hodder, 2019)

evaluation.name: Evaluation
evaluation.rule: Evaluate how the sample, measurement error and bias affect the reliability and scope of the conclusion. For each limitation, suggest a realistic improvement, such as more data, repeat measurements or a different method.
examples: Repeat the counts at different times to test whether a single lunchtime count represents the whole day.

contrast.en: Reliability means consistent results when the study is repeated; validity means the method answers the intended question. Repeating a biased method repeats the error; it does not remove the bias.
contrast.ru: Надёжность (reliability) — постоянство результатов при повторении исследования; валидность (validity) — соответствие метода исследовательскому вопросу. Повторение смещённого метода воспроизводит ошибку, но не устраняет смещение.

tectonics.title: Plate tectonics
tectonics.body: A tectonic plate is a piece of the lithosphere: the crust and the rigid uppermost mantle. Plates move relative to each other at divergent, convergent and transform boundaries. Where two continental plates collide, the land is pushed up into mountains.

contrast.en: A continent is not a plate: one plate can include both continental and oceanic crust.
contrast.ru: Континент — не плита: одна плита может включать и континентальную, и океаническую кору.

urbanisation.title: Urbanisation
urbanisation.body: Urbanisation is an increase in the share of a population that lives in towns and cities. It happens when people move from rural areas for work, schools and services, and when the urban population has a higher rate of natural increase than the rural population. Fast growth raises demand for housing, water, energy and transport. If services cannot keep up, poor housing and crowded informal settlements can appear. For example, a village near a growing city may be added to the city’s boundary, so its residents become urban without moving.

contrast.en: Do not confuse the number of city dwellers with the urban share. The number can rise while the share falls, if the total population grows faster.
contrast.ru: Не путай число горожан и долю городского населения. Число горожан может расти, а доля — падать, если общее население растёт быстрее.

globalisation.title: Globalisation
items: Globalisation is the growth of links and interdependence between countries through trade, investment, migration, information and culture.

Transnational corporations (TNCs) run factories, offices and shops in several countries. They choose where to produce according to costs, skills and access to customers, so one company's decision can move jobs and change local markets.

For example, a car company may design cars in one country, make parts in several others and assemble them in another. Benefits and costs are not shared equally: a region may lose factory jobs, while shoppers may pay less for goods.

contrast.en: Globalisation describes links between countries, while development describes people's health, education and choices. Stronger links can improve lives, but they do not do so for everyone automatically.
contrast.ru: Глобализация описывает связи между странами, а развитие — здоровье, образование и возможность выбирать. Более тесные связи могут улучшить жизнь людей, но не делают этого автоматически для всех.

sustainable.title: Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
sustainable.body: Sustainable development means meeting today's needs without taking away future generations' ability to meet their own. The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a set of global goals agreed by the member states of the United Nations to put this into practice. They cover poverty, hunger, health, water, energy, consumption and partnerships between countries. The goals are linked, so progress in one area can help or slow another. Examples of goals: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy). Two more goals: SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals).

contrast.en: Do not confuse a goal, a target and an indicator: a goal is a broad aim, a target is a specific step within it, and an indicator is a measure of progress.
contrast.ru: Не путай цель, задачу и индикатор: цель — общий ориентир, задача (target) — конкретный шаг внутри цели, индикатор (indicator) — то, что измеряют, чтобы видеть прогресс.

biomes.title: World biomes
items: A biome is a large region with a broadly similar climate and vegetation, along with the animals and other organisms adapted to those conditions. Boundaries between biomes are often gradual, so different sources divide the world into biomes in different ways.
Tropical rainforest: warm, wet conditions favour dense forest. Savanna: a clear wet and dry season supports grasses with scattered trees.
Deserts: very little rain, so water is scarce; they can be hot or cold. Temperate forests: clear seasons and enough rain for trees; many trees lose their leaves in autumn.
Boreal forest (taiga): long, cold winters and mostly coniferous trees. Tundra: low-growing plants and a short growing season; permafrost is widespread in Arctic tundra.

contrast.en: Do not confuse a biome with an ecosystem: an ecosystem can be as small as a pond, while a biome is a large region described by its climate and vegetation.
contrast.ru: Не путай биом и экосистему: экосистема может быть маленькой, например пруд, а биом — большая область, которую описывают климатом и растительностью.

development.title: Human development
development.body: Human development means expanding people's capabilities, choices and freedoms so they can live lives they value. Health, education and access to resources matter, and so do taking part in public life and being free to make choices. The Human Development Index (HDI) combines life expectancy, years of schooling and income into one measure. Economic growth can support development, but its benefits may be shared unequally.

contrast.en: Do not confuse GDP (gross domestic product) with human development. GDP measures the value of final goods and services produced within an economy over a stated period, such as a year. Counting final output avoids counting intermediate inputs again. GDP alone does not show whether people are healthy, educated or free to choose.
contrast.ru: Не путай ВВП (gross domestic product, GDP) и человеческое развитие. ВВП показывает стоимость конечных товаров и услуг, произведённых внутри экономики за определённый период, например год. Промежуточную продукцию не прибавляют повторно к стоимости конечной. Сам по себе ВВП не показывает, здоровы ли люди, получили ли они образование и могут ли свободно выбирать.

rivers.title: Distinctive Landscapes — Rivers
rivers.intro: How rivers shape the land: from source to mouth, processes of erosion and transportation, landform formation, flooding and management.

bradshaw.title: Bradshaw Model
bradshaw.description: The Bradshaw model summarises common downstream trends: discharge, width, depth and mean velocity tend to increase, while gradient and typical sediment size tend to decrease. Downstream, the cross-sectional area (CSA) of the channel grows faster than the wetted perimeter, which is the length of bed and bank in contact with the water. As a result, the hydraulic radius (R = A/P, where A is the CSA in m² and P is the wetted perimeter in m) increases. R is measured in metres: for A = 4 m² and P = 8 m, R = 4 / 8 = 0.5 m. At comparable roughness and energy slope, a larger hydraulic radius generally allows faster mean flow. Radius alone does not determine velocity. These are tendencies, not laws; geology, tributaries, dams and water abstraction can interrupt them. Slider values are illustrative, not measurements or predictions.

course.title: River Course
course.description: The upper, middle and lower course describe positions along a river’s long profile, a graph of bed height from source to mouth. Many rivers have a steeper upper course and gentler lower course. Downcutting can form a V-shaped valley upstream, but a gentler downstream gradient does not by itself mean slower flow: discharge, channel shape and roughness also matter. Deposition occurs where local flow can no longer carry its sediment load. Base level is the limit towards which a river can erode, ultimately sea level or a local lake or receiving river. A fall in base level can promote renewed downcutting. Erosion, transport and deposition can occur in every course.

detailed.intro:
Erosion is the wearing away and removal of rock and soil by moving water. Transportation is the movement of this eroded material (the load) by the river. Deposition is the dropping of the load when the river no longer has enough energy to carry it, usually when its velocity falls.

Weathering breaks rock down in place, without moving it, in three ways: mechanical (freeze-thaw, root wedging), chemical (dissolution, hydrolysis) and biological (burrowing animals, plants). Weathering and other subaerial processes, which act on land above the water, supply the debris that rivers transport.

abrasion.name: Abrasion (corrasion)
abrasion.rule: Sediment carried by a river scrapes, grinds or strikes the bed and banks, wearing them away. The load acts as an abrasive tool.
examples: Gravel swirled in a bedrock hollow can grind a pothole.

contrast.en: Abrasion wears the channel bed and banks; attrition wears the transported fragments themselves. Coastal erosion is a broader setting with wave and current action, so do not use it as a synonym for river abrasion.
contrast.ru: Истирание русла наносами (abrasion) разрушает дно и берега; истирание и дробление обломков (attrition) изменяет сами переносимые камни. Морская абразия относится к разрушению берегов волнами и течениями: её нельзя подставлять вместо речного термина без учёта контекста.

attrition.name: Attrition
attrition.rule: Transported rock fragments collide with one another and the channel, chipping off edges and becoming smaller and usually rounder.
examples: A newly broken angular pebble becomes smoother during repeated transport; rock hardness also matters.

model.en: Research literature sometimes uses abrasion more broadly; identify the material being worn.
model.ru: В научной литературе термин «истирание» иногда понимают шире. Уточняй, какой материал стирается.

hydraulicAction.name: Hydraulic action
hydraulicAction.rule: The force and pressure fluctuations of moving water loosen and remove material from the bed or banks. Water entering cracks can help detach jointed rock.
examples: Fast turbulent water can remove loose bank material even without gravel grinding it.

contrast.en: Hydraulic action depends on the force of the water; abrasion depends on sediment striking or scraping the channel. Trapped air compressed in cracks is only one mechanism of hydraulic action.
contrast.ru: Гидравлическое действие (hydraulic action) зависит от силы воды, а истирание русла (abrasion) — от ударов и трения наносов о дно и берега. Сжатие воздуха в трещинах — лишь один из механизмов гидравлического действия.

solution.name: Solution (corrosion)
solution.rule: Soluble minerals dissolve through chemical interaction with river water and are removed in solution. Rainwater and soil water take up carbon dioxide and become slightly acidic, so they can dissolve carbonate minerals in limestone.
examples: Calcium and bicarbonate ions can leave a limestone reach in clear water.

contrast.en: Dissolving the bed is chemical erosion: the ions are carried away in solution. Weathering, by contrast, breaks rock down in place without moving it.
contrast.ru: Растворение дна — это эрозия: растворённые ионы уносятся водой. Выветривание (weathering) разрушает породу на месте, без переноса. Оно бывает механическим (замерзание воды в трещинах, расклинивание корнями), химическим (растворение, гидролиз) и биологическим (роющие животные, растения). Выветривание и другие субаэральные (subaerial) процессы, которые идут на суше над уровнем воды, поставляют обломки, которые потом переносит река.

traction.name: Traction
traction.rule:
Traction is the rolling or sliding of the largest particles, such as boulders and pebbles, along the river bed.

The water’s force pushes these heavy particles along the bottom. The larger the particle, the faster the water must flow to move it. Traction therefore needs a strong flow, such as a steep upland stream during a flood.
examples: After heavy rain, a mountain stream rolls pebbles and small boulders downstream along its bed.

contrast.en: Traction particles stay in contact with the bed; saltation particles leave it in short hops. The same grain can switch from one to the other as the flow speed changes.
contrast.ru: При волочении частицы остаются у самого дна; при сальтации они на короткое время отрываются от него. Одна и та же частица может переходить от одного вида к другому при изменении скорости потока.

sources.title: Steven Earle — Physical Geology, 2nd edition (BCcampus)
sources.section: 13.3 Stream erosion and deposition; Figures 13.3.1–13.3.3

saltation.name: Saltation
saltation.rule:
Saltation is the movement of smaller particles, such as sand grains and small pebbles, in short hops along the river bed.

Each grain is lifted by the flow, falls back to the bed and is lifted again. Faster water lifts grains higher and for longer, and larger grains need faster water to hop. Saltation sits between traction and suspension.
examples: On a sandy lowland river, grains of sand bounce downstream close to the bed.

contrast.en: Saltation means repeated bed contact; suspension keeps particles within the flow for longer.
contrast.ru: При сальтации частица снова касается дна; во взвеси она дольше остаётся внутри потока.

suspension.name: Suspension
suspension.rule:
Suspension is the carrying of fine solid particles, such as silt and clay, within the water.

Turbulence, the swirling movement of the water, keeps these particles from settling to the bed. Fine particles are small and settle slowly, so turbulence can easily keep them in the water. Faster, more turbulent water can keep even larger particles, such as fine sand, in suspension.
examples: After heavy rain, a river can look brown or yellow because it carries fine silt in suspension.

contrast.en: Suspended material remains solid; dissolved material exists as dissolved ions or molecules.
contrast.ru: Взвешенный материал остаётся твёрдым; растворённое вещество находится в виде ионов или молекул.

solution.name: Dissolved load (transport in solution)
solution.rule:
Dissolved substances, such as salts, move with the river water as separate ions or molecules.

They do not need turbulence to stay in the water, so grain size does not matter. How much dissolves depends on how soluble the rock is.
examples: Water draining salt-rich ground can look clear yet carry dissolved salts downstream.

contrast.en: Clear water can carry a substantial dissolved load. Deposition by settling applies to particles, not directly to dissolved ions.
contrast.ru: Прозрачная вода может переносить немало растворённых веществ. Отложение при оседании относится к частицам, а не напрямую к растворённым ионам.

stages.1: Hard rock overlies soft rock; soft rock is eroded faster
stages.2: A plunge pool forms at the base of the drop
stages.3: An overhang develops as soft rock is eroded back
stages.4: The overhang collapses and the waterfall retreats upstream, leaving a gorge: a narrow, deep valley with steep sides. The cycle then repeats further upstream.

meander.title: Meander & oxbow lake
meander.description: A meander is a river bend. Faster flow erodes the outer bank, while slower flow deposits sediment on the inner bank as a point bar, so the bend shifts outwards and downstream. During floods, the river spills onto the floodplain, the flat land beside the channel, and drops its coarsest load close to the banks, building up a levee, a natural embankment along the channel. When the neck of a bend narrows enough, the river cuts through it and the abandoned loop becomes an oxbow lake. Not every bend follows this sequence.

drainageBasin.title: Drainage basin
drainageBasin.description: A drainage basin (catchment) is the area that supplies water to a river through a common outlet. A drainage divide separates neighbouring basins. Some precipitation is intercepted by plants; the rest either soaks into the soil or runs over the surface. Water then reaches the river as throughflow, groundwater flow or surface runoff. Evaporation and transpiration return water to the atmosphere. Over a period with little storage change and no net external water input, runoff is therefore less than precipitation. During an individual dry period, however, river flow can continue from water stored earlier in soil, groundwater, lakes or snow.

hydrograph.title: Storm hydrograph
hydrograph.description: A hydrograph plots river discharge against time. A storm hydrograph shows the response to rainfall: the rising limb climbs to the peak discharge, the highest flow during the flood, and the falling limb brings the flow back towards normal. Lag time is the time from peak rainfall to peak discharge.

flooding.title: Causes of flooding
flooding.physical: Physical: intense or prolonged rain, saturated ground, snowmelt, steep slopes, impermeable rock
flooding.human: Human: deforestation, urbanisation, drained wetlands, narrowed river channels, climate change

prolongedRain.name: Intense or prolonged rainfall
prolongedRain.rule: Intense rain can exceed the infiltration rate, producing surface runoff. Prolonged rain can fill available soil storage and raise groundwater levels, increasing the runoff from later rain. Where this water reaches the river, discharge rises; the timing and size of the response depend on the catchment and storm.
examples: A short, violent storm over a bare, steep hillside can send a flash flood down a dry valley within hours. A long spell of steady rain over already soaked fields raises a river more slowly, over several days.

contrast.en: Intense rainfall means a large amount of rain per unit of time, not a large total. Prolonged rainfall lasts a long time and can fill the soil with water even when each hour is light.
contrast.ru: Сильные осадки — это большой объём дождя за единицу времени, а не общая сумма. Длительные осадки идут долго и могут заполнить почву водой, даже если за каждый час выпадает немного.

saturatedGround.name: Antecedent conditions and saturation
saturatedGround.rule: Wet soil has less empty pore space available for additional storage. Where the ground is saturated and rainfall cannot drain into deeper layers fast enough, more water can run over the surface. This can increase flood response during wet periods, but drainage, rainfall and catchment storage still matter.
examples: Other conditions being similar, wet soil has less remaining storage than unsaturated soil, so the same storm may produce more rapid runoff. Dry soil does not guarantee infiltration: intense rain, compaction or water repellency can also cause runoff.

contrast.en: Saturation means the pores of soil or rock are full of water, while impermeability means water moves through a material only with great difficulty. Saturated sand, for example, can still let water through.
contrast.ru: Насыщение — это когда поры почвы или породы полностью заполнены водой, а непроницаемость — когда вода с большим трудом проходит сквозь материал. Насыщенный песок, например, всё ещё пропускает воду.

snowmelt.name: Snowmelt
snowmelt.rule: Melting releases water that was stored as snow. Rapid warming, or rain falling on snow, can send large volumes of meltwater into rivers within a short time. Frozen ground absorbs little of this water, so floods become more likely when warm spells or rain arrive early in spring.
examples: Snow melting on distant mountains can raise a lowland river for weeks in spring, even when no heavy rain falls near the river.

contrast.en: Snowfall only stores water, so the flood depends on when the snow melts and whether the ground can absorb the meltwater.
contrast.ru: Снегопад только копит воду, поэтому паводок зависит от того, когда снег растает и может ли грунт впитать талую воду.

reliefRock.name: Steep slopes, basin shape and soils
reliefRock.rule: Steep slopes can shorten runoff travel time. Low-permeability ground, such as many clay-rich soils, can restrict infiltration. Under comparable rainfall and other catchment conditions, a compact basin may concentrate runoff more closely in time than an elongated basin. However, the drainage network, storm location and movement, storage and channel capacity also affect the flood peak; shape alone does not establish flood frequency.
examples: Steep fields of clay soil above a village can send water from a heavy storm into the stream within a short time.

review.englishTerm: Steep slopes, basin shape and soils
review.russianTerm: Крутые склоны, форма бассейна и почвы

contrast.en: Relief is the shape of the land surface. A steep slope alone does not guarantee a flood, because vegetation, soils, drainage and the place where the storm falls also matter.
contrast.ru: Рельеф — это форма земной поверхности. Крутой склон сам по себе не гарантирует паводок: важны растительность, почвы, дренаж и место, где прошёл ливень.

deforestation.name: Deforestation and runoff
deforestation.rule: Leaves intercept some rain, part of which evaporates directly. Trees also take up soil water and release it by transpiration. Removing woodland can reduce these losses; logging machinery may compact soil and restrict infiltration. These changes can increase rapid runoff, but the flood response depends on soils, forest type, catchment scale, season and storm size.
examples: Ruts from logging machines on a forest track can turn the track into a channel that carries rainwater straight down the slope to a stream.

contrast.en: Deforestation means removing trees. Its effect depends on catchment size, soils and storm size, and trees cannot prevent every flood.
contrast.ru: Обезлесение — это вырубка деревьев. Эффект зависит от масштаба бассейна, почв и силы дождя; лес не предотвращает любой паводок.

urbanisation.name: Urbanisation and runoff
urbanisation.rule: Impervious surfaces reduce infiltration. If storm drains carry the extra runoff rapidly into a river, its storm peak can arrive sooner and be higher than under otherwise comparable permeable conditions. The result also depends on rainfall, storage and drainage design, so it is not inevitable after every storm.
examples: When a meadow beside a town is paved for a car park, rain that once soaked in now runs straight into storm drains, and the nearby river rises much faster.

contrast.en: Urbanisation means a growing share of people living in towns. Its flood effect depends less on the number of people than on sealed surfaces and storm drains.
contrast.ru: Урбанизация — это рост доли людей, живущих в городах. Влияние на паводки связано не столько с числом жителей, сколько с асфальтом, бетоном и ливневой канализацией.

climate.name: Climate change and flood risk
climate.rule: Warmer air holds more water vapour, so heavy downpours can become more intense and frequent in many regions. Climate change therefore alters the flood hazard. Losses depend on exposure (how many people and buildings lie in the flood path) and vulnerability (how easily they can be harmed).
examples: The same heavy storm may flood a paved town centre but only soak into a wooded hillside upstream.

contrast.en: Climate change is a long-term shift in weather patterns, including heavier downpours in many places. A global trend does not mean every river will flood more often, because regional weather and changes within each catchment matter.
contrast.ru: Изменение климата — это долгосрочный сдвиг погодных условий, в том числе более сильные ливни во многих местах. Глобальная тенденция не значит, что каждая река будет чаще выходить из берегов: важны региональная погода и изменения в водосборном бассейне.

management.title: Management strategies
management.hard: Hard engineering: dams, embankments, channel straightening, flood walls
management.soft: Soft engineering: floodplain zoning, afforestation, river restoration, flood warnings. Soft methods usually complement hard ones rather than replace them, and their effect in extreme floods is still poorly understood.

dams.name: Dams and reservoirs
dams.rule: A dam holds back river water, and the reservoir behind it stores part of a flood. The stored water is then released slowly, so the peak flow downstream is lower. Dams are expensive to build and change the natural flow of the river.
examples: A dam holds back floodwater in its reservoir and lowers the peak flow downstream. The reservoir also traps sediment, so the riverbed below the dam can be eroded and the delta receives less sediment. People living on land that the reservoir floods may have to move.

contrast.en: A reservoir can store floodwater only if it has spare capacity. A full reservoir cannot hold any more water.
contrast.ru: Водохранилище может накопить паводковую воду, только если в нём есть свободный объём. Полное водохранилище уже не может принять воду.

embankments.name: Flood embankments (artificial levees)
embankments.rule: A flood embankment is a raised earth bank along a river. It protects the land behind it from floodwater, but only up to its design height. When an embankment cuts off the floodplain from the river, water in the channel moves faster and rises higher, so the risk often passes downstream. Building and repairing embankments is expensive.
examples: Along a river that carries a heavy load of sediment, the bed can rise above the surrounding plain. Embankments then have to be raised again and again. When an embankment breaks, water floods large areas.

contrast.en: Artificial embankments differ from natural levees, which form when a river deposits sediment on its banks during floods.
contrast.ru: Искусственные защитные дамбы отличаются от естественных прирусловых валов (natural levees), которые возникают, когда река откладывает наносы на берегах во время разливов.

channelStraightening.name: Channel straightening
channelStraightening.rule: Cutting off bends shortens the channel, so the same drop in height now happens over a shorter distance. The slope becomes steeper and the water speeds up through that section.
examples: A river may be straightened into a canal. Its bends are lost, floodplain wetlands are drained, and the birds that depended on those wetlands become less common. Later, some lost bends may be restored.

contrast.en: Straightening speeds up water on one stretch but does not make the whole river safer, because floodwater reaches towns downstream sooner.
contrast.ru: Спрямление ускоряет воду на одном участке, но не делает реку безопаснее в целом: паводок быстрее доходит до населённых пунктов ниже по течению.

floodWalls.name: Flood walls
floodWalls.rule: A flood wall is a barrier of concrete, steel or stone built along a river or around buildings. It protects the area only up to its design height, and water above that level spills over the top.
examples: In a city centre with no room for a wide earth embankment, a wall can protect the buildings. It still needs regular inspection, because cracks and loose joints let water through.

contrast.en: A wall keeps river floodwater out, but rain that collects behind the wall must be drained away separately.
contrast.ru: Стена не пускает речную воду на защищаемую территорию, но дождевую воду, которая собирается за стеной, нужно отводить отдельно.

floodplainZoning.name: Floodplain zoning
floodplainZoning.rule: Floodplain zoning limits building on areas that often flood. Such land can be kept free for floodwater, or used for activities that suffer less damage, such as parks and sports fields.
examples: A riverside park may tolerate temporary inundation better than a hospital on the same site.

contrast.en: Zoning mainly reduces exposure; it does not stop the river rising.
contrast.ru: Зонирование прежде всего уменьшает подверженность; уровень реки при этом всё равно может расти.

afforestation.name: Afforestation and catchment woodland
afforestation.rule: Tree canopies catch some rain, and roots open up the soil, so more water soaks in and less runs off quickly. The effect is largest for small floods in small catchments and weakens as floods get bigger.
examples: In a small catchment planted with trees, the soil under the woodland soaks up more rain than the grazed fields around it, so less water runs off in small storms.

contrast.en: Afforestation means planting trees on land that has not recently been forest. Reforestation means replanting where forest was recently cut down or burnt.
contrast.ru: Лесоразведение (afforestation) — посадка леса на земле, где лес давно не рос. Лесовосстановление (reforestation) — восстановление леса на месте недавней вырубки или пожара.

restoration.name: River restoration
restoration.rule: Restoring the channel lets the river spread across its floodplain again. Part of a flood is then stored there, so less water reaches towns downstream at once. The effect depends on how long the restored stretch is compared with the size of the whole catchment. Bends and wetlands also return, which improves conditions for plants and animals.
examples: Where flood embankments are removed, water spreads across the floodplain at high flows, so the peak downstream falls, though often only slightly.

contrast.en: Restoration does not mean flooding is eliminated; some land is deliberately allowed to flood to reduce damage elsewhere.
contrast.ru: Восстановление не устраняет затопление: часть земли намеренно оставляют для разлива, снижая ущерб в других местах.

warnings.name: Flood forecasts and warnings
warnings.rule: A forecast estimates when and where a river may rise, based on observations and models. A warning passes this on with clear advice, so people have time to prepare. Forecasts are estimates, so they are never completely certain.
examples: A warning system may use several levels. Each level tells people what to do, such as moving possessions upstairs or leaving before the roads flood.

contrast.en: A warning reduces consequences only if it reaches people in time and they can act; it does not reduce the rainfall itself.
contrast.ru: Предупреждение уменьшает последствия, если приходит вовремя и люди могут действовать; сам дождь оно не ослабляет.

boscastle.title: Case study — Boscastle floods 2004
boscastle.summary: On 16 August 2004, intense rain fell on the steep slopes around Boscastle, Cornwall. Water ran off the land quickly, and the rivers overtopped. A flash flood swept through the village. Buildings were damaged and vehicles were carried away. No one died, but a major helicopter rescue operation was needed.

seep.social: Social: people needed urgent rescue and evacuation, and temporary shelter was required.
seep.economic: Economic: homes, businesses, roads and bridges were damaged, and vehicles were swept away.
seep.environmental: Environmental: floodwater moved large amounts of sediment and debris, which then had to be cleared away.
seep.political: Political: the flood exposed weaknesses in local flood planning.

responses.local: Local: emergency services carried out the rescues; affected people were given emergency shelter.
responses.government: Government and partners: local councils and other organisations took part in the village’s post-flood regeneration.
responses.shortTerm: Short term: flood debris was removed from the village.
responses.longTerm: Long term: flood defence schemes were introduced in the village.

tourism.title: Tourism
tourism.intro: Types of tourism, the Butler model of how destinations change over time, and case studies of mass and niche tourism.

mass.name: Mass tourism
mass.rule: Tourism involving large visitor flows and services organised on a large scale, often concentrated in popular resorts and supported by standardised transport and accommodation.
examples: For example, coastal resorts with large hotels and package holidays show the pattern; visitor numbers alone do not show how much local people gain.

contrast.en: Mass describes scale and organisation, not a traveller's motive; many visitors can still have different interests.
contrast.ru: «Массовый» описывает масштаб и организацию, а не мотив: интересы многочисленных посетителей могут различаться.

sources.title: BCcampus — Introduction to Tourism and Hospitality in BC
sources.section: Chapter 1: history and overview; mass tourism and tourism impacts

thanatourism.name: Dark tourism / thanatourism
thanatourism.rule: Dark tourism, or thanatourism, is travel to places linked with death, suffering or disaster, such as memorials and former sites of violence. Remembrance and learning are common motives, but not every visitor has them.
examples: For example, guided visits to a memorial on the site of a former camp need careful explanation and respect for the victims.

contrast.en: Dark tourism and thanatourism are often used as synonyms, but some researchers limit thanatourism to trips motivated by encounters with death.
contrast.ru: Тёмный туризм и танатуризм часто используют как синонимы, но некоторые исследователи сужают танатуризм до поездок, мотивированных встречей со смертью.

sources.title: Philip R. Stone — A Dark Tourism Spectrum (2006)
sources.section: Introduction and dark tourism supply/demand, pp. 146–147

ecotourism.name: Ecotourism
ecotourism.rule: Ecotourism is nature-based travel in which visitors mainly come to see and appreciate nature. It includes learning, keeps environmental and cultural damage low, and supports conservation and local communities.
examples: For example, on a small island reserve, visitors usually walk with a licensed guide on designated trails, which limits damage to fragile habitats.

contrast.en: A trip into nature is not ecotourism by default; check who manages it, whether it helps conservation and whether local people take part.
contrast.ru: Поход в природу сам по себе не экотуризм: проверь, кто управляет объектом, помогает ли он охране природы и участвуют ли в нём местные жители.

sources.title: UN Tourism — Ecotourism and protected areas

medical.name: Medical tourism
medical.rule: Medical tourism is travel to receive healthcare, such as diagnosis, treatment or rehabilitation, away from home. The trip can be domestic or across a border.
examples: For example, some patients travel abroad for dental or cosmetic treatment; the country alone does not establish price, quality or safety.

contrast.en: Medical tourism is about treatment; wellness tourism is mainly about staying healthy and may involve no treatment at all.
contrast.ru: Медицинский туризм связан с лечением; оздоровительный туризм в первую очередь направлен на поддержание самочувствия и может обходиться без лечения.

extreme.name: Adventure and extreme tourism
extreme.rule: Adventure tourism is usually defined as a trip that combines at least two of three elements: physical activity, a natural environment and cultural immersion. Extreme tourism is the most demanding or dangerous part of that range.
examples: For example, an expedition to Antarctica involves ice, cold and distance from help, while a short walk on a marked coastal path does not.

contrast.en: A guided walk on lowland paths and a high-altitude climb may both count as adventure tourism, yet they need very different skills and safety measures.
contrast.ru: Прогулка с гидом по равнине и подъём на большую высоту могут считаться приключенческим туризмом, но требуют очень разных навыков и мер безопасности.

voluntourism.name: Voluntourism
voluntourism.rule: Voluntourism combines a holiday with voluntary work on a local project, often through a paid programme. Its benefit depends on whether the work meets the real needs of the host community and the skills of the volunteer.
examples: For example, a biogas plant that local residents asked for, built by trained volunteers working alongside local staff, has a clear purpose; a short visit to 'help' with no clear task does not.

contrast.en: Good intentions or a paid fee do not prove that a project helps; volunteers should meet local needs rather than replace paid local workers.
contrast.ru: Добрые намерения или плата за участие не доказывают, что проект полезен: волонтёры должны отвечать на местные потребности, а не вытеснять оплачиваемых местных работников.

nature.name: Nature and wildlife tourism
nature.rule: Travel primarily to experience natural landscapes, plants or wild animals. It describes the attraction and visitor activity.
examples: Whale watching is nature tourism; its ecological effects depend on how boats and visitors behave.

contrast.en: Ecotourism adds conservation, learning and community-benefit requirements; wildlife viewing alone does not meet them.
contrast.ru: Экотуризм добавляет требования охраны природы, обучения и пользы для жителей; одного наблюдения за животными недостаточно.

butler.title: Butler model (tourism area life cycle)

stages.5: Stagnation — growth slows or levels off; environmental or service capacity may be strained
stages.6: Possible later paths — decline or rejuvenation; none is inevitable

butler.examples: The tourism-area life-cycle is a conceptual model of possible destination change. Stages can overlap, be interrupted or follow different paths. The curve is schematic: neither time nor visitor numbers are calibrated.

jamaica.title: Case study: mass tourism on a small island
jamaica.facts: On many small island countries, tourism is one of the most important industries. Overnight guests often spend more on accommodation and local services than cruise passengers, who may spend only a day ashore. When you judge the value of tourism, separate the direct effect (what visitors spend) from the total effect (including suppliers and wages that also depend on tourism).
jamaica.attractions: A warm tropical island attracts visitors with its beaches. Coastal areas offer water sports, and some resorts sell all-inclusive packages.
jamaica.positives: Tourism can create jobs, demand for local goods, tax income and money for infrastructure, such as roads and water supply. Local people gain more when they own businesses, sell goods to hotels and have skilled jobs in the tourism sector.
jamaica.negatives: Mass tourism can cause income leakage: foreign-owned hotels may send profits abroad, and goods for visitors are often imported. Work is often seasonal, so many people earn little in quieter months. In the peak season, demand for water, electricity and housing can overload local services. Building on the coast can damage habitats, and traditions shown to visitors can turn into products, which changes local culture. Effects differ from place to place, so check each case.
jamaica.management: Management can reduce these effects. Governments may regulate new development, including building on the coast. Community tourism programmes can give local people a share of the income and a say in what is offered. All-inclusive resorts are debated because guests spend inside the complex, so less money reaches local businesses.

antarctica.title: Case study — Antarctica (extreme tourism)
antarctica.facts: Antarctica has no permanent resident population. Research stations are staffed by scientists and support staff, while tourists usually visit during the southern summer. Remoteness, ice and fast-changing weather make access difficult and rescue slow.
antarctica.whyGrowing: Specialist ships and organised expeditions make visits to Antarctica possible. Interest in remote, wild landscapes and wildlife can attract more and more visitors. The more people visit, the greater the pressure on sensitive sites, such as penguin colonies.
antarctica.negatives: Tourism can disturb wildlife: noise, crowds and close approach may disrupt feeding and breeding, and some birds may abandon their nests. Non-native organisms carried on boots, clothing or equipment can establish themselves and harm native species. Ships and aircraft produce emissions, and waste or fuel spills can damage the environment. Oil harms penguins through their feathers: oiled feathers lose their insulation and their ability to repel water, so the birds get cold and swim poorly.
antarctica.positives: Tourism brings income to tour operators and crew, and some expeditions include talks on science and conservation. Visitors who see the landscape first-hand may become more aware of climate change and of the need to protect the region.
antarctica.management: Tourism is regulated by the Antarctic Treaty system and by national permits. Members of IAATO, the International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators, follow its rules on visitor behaviour. Its guidance asks visitors to keep their distance from wildlife, not to feed animals and to take all their waste away. Some protected areas need a special permit, and clean boots and clothing stop seeds and other organisms being carried in.

thana.name: Dark tourism — applying the definition
thana.rule: Use the definition above: is the main purpose of this trip to visit a place linked to death, suffering or disaster?
examples: For example, an ancient amphitheatre was an arena where gladiators fought and where people and animals were killed for public entertainment. A tour that focuses on these deaths, not only on the building, fits the definition of dark tourism.

contrast.en: A visit to learn about a disaster and honour its victims is a clear example. A visitor taking photographs at the same site may have different motives. That alone does not exclude the visit from the broader dark-tourism category; a motive-based definition of thanatourism asks specifically about an interest in death.
contrast.ru: Поездка ради изучения катастрофы и памяти её жертв — ясный пример. У посетителя, который фотографирует то же место, могут быть другие мотивы. Само по себе это не исключает поездку из широкой категории тёмного туризма; определение танатуризма через мотив специально учитывает интерес к смерти.

medical.name: Medical tourism — applying the definition
medical.rule: Compare two trips: one for an operation and one to visit a relative in hospital. Which traveller is receiving medical care?
examples: A patient from abroad books a planned operation at a specialist clinic in a neighbouring country, after checking the clinic’s accreditation.

contrast.en: Test the follow-up: check who will care for the patient when they return home, because complications can appear after the trip.
contrast.ru: Проверь наблюдение после лечения: кто будет наблюдать пациента, когда он вернётся домой, ведь осложнения могут появиться уже после поездки.

eco.name: Ecotourism — applying the definition
eco.rule: An operator advertises a nature tour. What evidence would you request before accepting its environmental claims?
examples: In this example, a local community runs guided walks in a forest reserve and uses part of the fees to fund conservation, while retaining income locally.

volun.name: Voluntourism — applying the definition
volun.rule: A visitor offers to teach for one day. Explain what the host community should check before accepting the offer.
examples: For example, at the request of a village, volunteers help install a water filter, and local staff learn how to maintain it. The purpose is clear from the start, and the result stays in the village.

contrast.en: Test the project: ask who keeps the skills and the result after the volunteers leave.
contrast.ru: Проверь проект: кто сохранит навыки и результат после отъезда волонтёров.

extreme.name: Extreme tourism — applying the definition
extreme.rule: Compare a marked lowland walk with a remote high-altitude climb. Explain how access to rescue changes the risk.
examples: A solo cave dive far from the entrance carries a high risk of injury or death, because there is no easy exit and no quick help. A supervised dive in shallow open water carries a much lower risk.

contrast.en: Test the risk: ask whether a rescue would arrive in time to help a serious injury, and whether the guide can stop the trip.
contrast.ru: Проверь риск: успеет ли спасение помочь при тяжёлой травме и может ли гид остановить поездку.

resourceReliance.title: Resource reliance
resourceReliance.intro: Societies depend on resources such as energy, water and food. This topic covers sustainability, the theories of Malthus and Boserup, and the key players who shape how resources are distributed and used.

resource.name: Resource
resource.rule: A resource is anything from the natural environment that people use to meet a need or achieve a goal, such as water, soil, minerals or sunlight. Something becomes a resource only when people have the technology and access to use it, so what counts as a resource can change over time. Supply is the amount of a resource that is available to use. Demand is the wish to buy a resource, backed by the ability to pay for it.
examples: A forest can provide a continuing supply of timber if harvesting does not exceed regrowth and ecosystem functions are maintained. Overuse can deplete this renewable resource. Uranium, used as nuclear fuel, is a finite mineral resource.

contrast.en: Renewable resources can still be depleted if use exceeds regeneration. Flow resources, such as sunlight, are not finite deposits like oil.
contrast.ru: Возобновляемые ресурсы тоже можно истощить, если использование превышает восстановление. Потоковые ресурсы (flow resources), например солнечный свет, в отличие от нефти, не образуют конечных месторождений.

consumption.name: Resource consumption
consumption.rule: Consumption is the use of resources by people and economic activities over a stated period. Total use shows the overall strain on a resource, while use per person shows how much one person uses on average. A country with a large population can have a high total use even when each person uses little, so both measures are needed when comparing countries.
examples: Water for irrigating crops counts towards a country's total water use. A country with large irrigated farms can therefore have a high total use even if each household uses little water.

contrast.en: A country can cut its own extraction of a resource while its consumption stays high through imports.
contrast.ru: Страна может сократить собственную добычу ресурса, но её потребление останется высоким за счёт импорта.

carrying.name: Carrying capacity
carrying.rule: Carrying capacity is the population an environment can support over time under stated resource and consumption conditions. In the simple logistic model, a population starting well below a constant carrying capacity grows slowly at first, then faster, and finally slows as it approaches that limit, forming an S-shaped curve. Real populations can fluctuate or overshoot, and the limit itself can change.
examples: Groundwater in a farming valley: if farmers pump it faster than rain and rivers refill it, the valley can no longer support the same number of farms and people.

contrast.en: For people, carrying capacity depends on technology and consumption, so it changes over time. It is not a fixed number of people for the whole planet.
contrast.ru: Для людей ёмкость среды зависит от технологий и уровня потребления, поэтому со временем меняется. Это не фиксированное число жителей Земли.

sustainability.title: Sustainability
sustainability.brundtland: Sustainability asks whether today's use of resources can continue without depleting them for future generations. The answer depends on the carrying capacity of the environment and on how fairly resources are shared.
sustainability.sdgs: Four of the 17 SDGs are especially relevant to resource reliance: Goal 2 (zero hunger), Goal 6 (clean water and sanitation), Goal 7 (affordable and clean energy) and Goal 12 (responsible consumption and production).

brundtland.name: Sustainable development (Brundtland definition)
brundtland.rule: Sustainable development meets present needs without reducing the ability of future generations to meet theirs. For a renewable resource, this means using it no faster than it can regenerate, and keeping total use within the carrying capacity of the environment. For a finite resource, it means using it more slowly and finding alternatives.
examples: A fishery that keeps its catch below the rate at which fish regrow can feed people now and still leave fish for future generations.

contrast.en: Sustainable development is broader than environmental protection or continuing GDP growth; examine social, economic and environmental outcomes together.
contrast.ru: Устойчивое развитие шире охраны природы или непрерывного роста ВВП (GDP); рассматривай социальные, экономические и экологические результаты вместе.

sdgs.name: Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
sdgs.rule: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are 17 global goals adopted by UN member states as part of the UN Agenda for Sustainable Development. Each goal has targets and indicators that make progress measurable.
examples: A town that treats its sewage before it reaches a river contributes to Goal 6, which covers water and sanitation.

contrast.en: A goal is an intended outcome; adoption does not show that the outcome has been achieved.
contrast.ru: Цель — это желаемый результат. Принятие цели не доказывает, что результат уже достигнут.

energy.title: Energy sources
energy.renewable: Renewable energy sources are replenished naturally on a human timescale. The main ones are solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal and biomass.
energy.nonRenewable: Non-renewable energy sources are not replenished on a human timescale. The main ones are coal, oil, natural gas and the uranium used as fuel in nuclear power stations.

solar.name: Solar energy
solar.rule: Solar energy is energy from the Sun's light and heat. Photovoltaic cells convert light directly into electricity. Solar thermal systems collect heat, or use mirrors to focus sunlight and heat water into steam that drives a turbine.
examples: A rooftop solar panel makes electricity without burning fuel, but it produces no electricity at night.

contrast.en: Solar is renewable, but output varies with daylight and weather; installed capacity is not continuous generation.
contrast.ru: Солнечная энергия возобновляема, но выработка меняется с освещением и погодой; установленная мощность не равна постоянной выработке.

wind.name: Wind energy
wind.rule: Wind energy is the kinetic energy of moving air. Wind turbines use it to turn their blades, and a generator then converts that rotation into electricity. Wind is replenished because the Sun heats the Earth's surface unevenly, which makes air move.
examples: A wind farm makes electricity without burning fuel, but its turbines need large areas of land and can change the local landscape.

contrast.en: Wind speed and turbine operating limits determine output; turbines do not generate their rated power all the time.
contrast.ru: Выработка зависит от скорости ветра и рабочих ограничений турбины; турбина не всегда работает на номинальной мощности.

hydro.name: Hydropower
hydro.rule: Hydropower generates electricity when flowing water turns turbines. Dams often hold back water, so it falls through the turbines from a higher level. The water cycle, driven by the Sun, keeps refilling rivers and reservoirs.
examples: A reservoir can store water and release it when more electricity is needed, but in a dry year less water flows in and less electricity is made.

contrast.en: Renewable does not mean impact-free: dams alter sediment, habitats and land use; drought can reduce generation.
contrast.ru: Возобновляемое не означает безвредное: плотины меняют наносы, местообитания и землепользование; засуха может снизить выработку.

geothermal.name: Geothermal energy
geothermal.rule: Geothermal energy is heat from inside the Earth. It is used directly for heating, or to generate electricity where the underground water or rock is hot enough.
examples: In some volcanic regions, hot water from underground heats homes without burning fuel.

contrast.en: A renewable classification does not guarantee every local reservoir is inexhaustible; extraction and recharge must be managed.
contrast.ru: Возобновляемость не значит, что каждый подземный резервуар неисчерпаем: его отбор и восполнение нужно контролировать.

biofuels.name: Biofuels and biomass
biofuels.rule: Biomass is organic material from recently living plants and animals, such as wood, crop residues or manure. Biofuels are fuels made from biomass, for example ethanol, biodiesel and biogas. The energy in biomass is sunlight that plants stored through photosynthesis.
examples: Some countries make ethanol from sugar cane to fuel cars, but fuel crops can compete with food crops for land.

contrast.en: Renewability requires replacement of the biomass; carbon emissions depend on cultivation, land-use change, processing and combustion.
contrast.ru: Возобновляемость требует восстановления биомассы; выбросы зависят от выращивания, изменения землепользования, переработки и сжигания.

fossilFuels.name: Fossil fuels
fossilFuels.rule: Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels. They formed from the remains of ancient organic material over geological time. Burning them releases the chemical energy stored in them, together with carbon dioxide.
examples: A gas-fired power station can be switched on when demand rises, but burning the gas still releases CO₂.

contrast.en: They are non-renewable on a human timescale: a large deposit does not make them renewable.
contrast.ru: В масштабах человеческой жизни они невозобновляемы: большое месторождение не делает их возобновляемыми.

nuclear.name: Nuclear fission energy
nuclear.rule: Nuclear power stations release energy by splitting heavy atomic nuclei (fission), usually of uranium. The heat boils water into steam, and the steam turns turbines that generate electricity.
examples: Some countries generate much of their electricity in nuclear power stations. They emit little CO₂ during operation, but they produce radioactive waste that must be stored safely for a very long time.

contrast.en: Nuclear power is generally considered low-carbon over its life cycle, but it uses finite fuel and creates waste that needs long-term management. Low-carbon and renewable are different categories.
contrast.ru: Атомную энергетику обычно считают низкоуглеродной за весь жизненный цикл, но она использует конечное минеральное топливо и создаёт отходы, которые нужно долго хранить и контролировать. Низкоуглеродность и возобновляемость — разные категории.

malthusBoserup.title: Malthus and Boserup: two theories
malthusBoserup.malthus: Malthus argued that population tends to grow faster than food supply, so checks such as famine and disease would limit growth.
malthusBoserup.boserup: Boserup argued that population pressure can push farmers to use their land more intensively, which can raise output per unit of land.

malthus.name: Malthusian population model
malthus.rule: Malthus argued that population tends to outgrow food supply unless checked, under his assumptions about their relative growth. Preventive checks, such as postponing marriage, can reduce births before a crisis; positive checks, including famine, disease and war, raise deaths. This is a historical model, not a universal forecast.
examples: In a village where more children survive each year, more people share the same fields. If the harvest does not grow, each person gets less food, which is the kind of pressure Malthus described.

contrast.en: A model of population pressure does not explain every famine: access, unequal distribution, conflict and technology also matter.
contrast.ru: Модель демографического давления не объясняет каждый голод: важны доступ, неравенство, конфликты и технологии.

boserup.name: Boserup's agricultural intensification model
boserup.rule: Boserup proposed that population pressure on a given land area can encourage more intensive farming: shorter fallows, more frequent cropping, additional labour and techniques such as irrigation. This can raise annual output from the land while requiring more work; output per harvest or per hour of labour need not rise. Investment, skills and environmental conditions limit the response.
examples: A farmer who sows a new crop straight after the harvest, instead of leaving the field to rest, can feed more people from the same land. That farmer now spends more time ploughing, weeding and watering.

contrast.en: Higher output per hectare need not mean higher output per hour of labour. New techniques are not automatic, and they can bring environmental costs, such as soil damage.
contrast.ru: Больший выпуск с гектара не обязательно означает больший выпуск за час труда. Новые методы не появляются сами собой, и они могут нанести ущерб окружающей среде, например истощить почву.

waterStress.title: Water stress
waterStress.description: Water stress is the strain that water use places on the water that is available. It is high when people, farms and factories take a large share of the water that rivers and groundwater can renew.

definition.name: Water stress
definition.rule: Water stress measures pressure from water use on available freshwater. SDG indicator 6.4.2 is freshwater withdrawal as a percentage of renewable freshwater resources after allowing for environmental water requirements. Compare withdrawals and resources for the same place and period.
examples: In a dry summer, a river carries much less water, while farms in its valley still want to irrigate. The valley can be under water stress even when the national annual average looks fine.

contrast.en: Water stress is a measure of strain; water security is broader and includes reliable access, water quality, ecosystems and protection from water-related harm. Different indices may use different thresholds.
contrast.ru: Водный стресс — это показатель нагрузки. Водная безопасность (water security) шире: она включает надёжный доступ к воде, её качество, экосистемы и защиту от вреда, связанного с водой. Разные индексы могут использовать разные пороговые значения.

causes.name: Drivers of water stress
causes.rule: Stress can rise when withdrawals increase, renewable supply falls, or water needed by ecosystems is left out of allocation. Irrigation, industry, households and drought all affect the balance.
examples: Expanding irrigation without a water budget can raise withdrawals beyond sustainable availability.

contrast.en: Scarce rainfall is only one cause; high demand can stress a relatively wet basin, while poor water quality can restrict usable supply.
contrast.ru: Недостаток осадков — лишь одна из причин: высокий спрос может создать нагрузку даже на относительно влажный бассейн, а низкое качество воды может сокращать запасы, пригодные для использования.

solutions.name: Managing water stress
solutions.rule: Combine demand management, cutting leakage, appropriate reuse, protection of water quality and ecosystems, and reliable supply planning at basin scale.
examples: Repairing leaking pipes in a city means less water is taken from a river for the same supply, but the repairs cost money.

contrast.en: More efficient irrigation does not automatically save water across a basin if saved water expands irrigated area or reduces return flows.
contrast.ru: Более эффективное орошение не экономит воду в масштабе бассейна автоматически. Экономии может не быть, если сэкономленная вода идёт на расширение орошаемых площадей или уменьшает возвратный сток.

foodSecurity.title: Food security
foodSecurity.factors: Population, water, climate, soils, incomes, conflict and trade all affect availability, access, utilisation and stability, but in different ways.

definition.name: Food security
definition.rule: People have food security when they can consistently obtain enough safe, nutritious food for a healthy active life. Four connected dimensions are availability, access, utilisation and stability over time.
examples: A drought that cuts the local harvest reduces availability, because less food reaches the market. A family whose income falls can lose access to food.

contrast.en: A country can produce enough food while some households cannot afford it. Food insecurity is broader than famine and is not the same as low national self-sufficiency.
contrast.ru: Страна может производить достаточно пищи, но часть семей не может её купить. Продовольственная незащищённость шире массового голода и не равна низкому самообеспечению страны.

drivers.name: Drivers of food insecurity
drivers.rule: Crop losses can reduce availability. Conflict, displacement or low income can block access. Unsafe water or a poor diet can impair utilisation. Repeated shocks undermine stability.
examples: A price rise may make food inaccessible to low-income households without a complete production failure.

contrast.en: Food insecurity can occur where shops contain food. Identify which dimension fails rather than assuming too little food is grown.
contrast.ru: Продовольственная незащищённость возможна и там, где в магазинах полно еды. Определи, какое измерение нарушено, а не предполагай, что еды выращивают слишком мало.

solutions.name: Improving food security
solutions.rule: Match action to the failing dimension: resilient farming and storage support availability; income or food assistance support access; safe water and good nutrition support utilisation; planning helps stability.
examples: A school meal programme gives children a reliable meal every school day. This supports their access to food and their nutrition.

contrast.en: Increasing yield alone cannot solve insecurity caused by lost income, exclusion or conflict.
contrast.ru: Одно повышение урожайности не устраняет проблемы из-за утраты дохода, исключения из доступа или конфликта.
