players.title: Key players
players.items: Five groups of players influence how resources are used: international organisations such as the United Nations (UN), non-governmental organisations (NGOs), businesses, national and local governments, and citizens and consumers. For example, these include the UN, an environmental NGO and a large supermarket chain. Together, their decisions largely determine whether resources can be used sustainably, that is, in a way that future generations can also use them.

un.name: United Nations and international agencies
un.rule: Intergovernmental organisations are made up of member states, so their decisions depend on agreement between governments. They help by setting shared goals, collecting evidence, giving technical assistance and running programmes that support sustainable resource use. Different UN bodies have different mandates and powers: some can only advise, while others can make binding decisions.
examples: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), a UN agency, publishes data on food and farming, so countries can compare how they use their land and water.

contrast.en: An agreed global goal is not the same as action in a country, because governments decide how to carry it out. Do not treat all UN bodies as one government.
contrast.ru: Согласованная глобальная цель — ещё не действия в стране: выполнение зависит от правительств. Нельзя считать все органы ООН одним правительством.

ngos.name: Non-governmental organisations (NGOs)
ngos.rule: Non-governmental organisations work outside government for public or community goals, for example through campaigning, research or services. They cannot make laws, so they influence resource use by persuading governments, businesses and the public. Their campaigns and research can help resource use become more sustainable. Funding and accountability arrangements vary between organisations, so their independence can differ.
examples: A community group runs a beach clean-up project. Its report should show whether residents helped plan the work, what measurements prove its results, and how it spent its money.

contrast.en: A non-governmental organisation does not have to rely only on donations, and it does not automatically speak for every local resident.
contrast.ru: Неправительственная организация не обязана получать деньги только от пожертвований и не обязательно представляет всех местных жителей.

businesses.name: Businesses and transnational corporations (TNCs)
businesses.rule: Businesses produce goods and services and decide how to use materials, energy and labour. A transnational corporation (TNC) organises or controls activities in more than one country. Its supply chains, investment and purchasing decisions affect resource use, jobs and pollution, so these decisions matter for sustainability. Laws, costs and customer demand limit what companies can change.
examples: A supermarket chain says it will cut the plastic packaging it uses. To check this claim, compare how much packaging it used in the year it made the pledge with the amount used in later years.

contrast.en: A company pledge is a stated intention; verified outcomes require a baseline, scope, dates and measured results.
contrast.ru: Обещание компании — заявленное намерение; подтверждённый результат требует исходного уровня (baseline), охвата, сроков и измеренных результатов.

governments.name: National and local governments
governments.rule: Governments can set rules, collect taxes, decide budgets and choose which infrastructure to build. Their choices are limited by budgets, by laws and by the capacity of their institutions, so their effectiveness differs from place to place. Long-term planning can protect water, energy and land for future use, so governments play a key part in sustainable resource management.
examples: A regional government sets a target to clean up a polluted river. To evaluate delivery, check whether responsibilities and funding are clear, whether pollution controls are implemented, and whether suitable water-quality monitoring shows improvement.

contrast.en: Announcing a policy differs from funding, enforcing and evaluating it.
contrast.ru: Объявление политики отличается от её финансирования, исполнения и оценки.

citizens.name: Citizens and consumers
citizens.rule: Citizens and consumers influence resource use through what they buy, how they use water and energy, and through voting, petitions and community action. Their choices are limited by income, by local services and by the products on sale. Many small choices together can make resource use more sustainable, and making sustainable options accessible can increase participation.
examples: A family sorts its rubbish, but recycling a material is much harder if the local waste service does not collect it.

contrast.en: Individual consumption choices and structural policy act at different scales and can reinforce each other.
contrast.ru: Личное потребление и системная политика действуют на разных уровнях и могут дополнять друг друга.

atmosphericHazards.intro: This topic covers climate zones, atmospheric circulation, tropical cyclones and droughts. The two detailed case studies are Typhoon Haiyan and the Millennium Drought.

climateZones.title: Climate zones
climateZones.items: Polar, Temperate, Arid, Tropical, Mediterranean, Mountainous

polar.name: Polar climate
polar.rule: Polar climate (Köppen group E) has a warmest monthly mean below 10°C. In the Peel et al. classification, tundra (ET) has a warmest monthly mean above 0°C; ice-cap (EF) has no monthly mean above 0°C. These are long-term averages, not limits on every day’s weather. Low solar angles help explain high-latitude cold, while elevation also matters.
examples: Compare the tundra of northern Siberia or northern Canada, where a short summer supports mosses and lichens, with the interior of Antarctica, where the ice stays frozen all year.

contrast.en: The polar circles are astronomical latitude lines, not exact climate boundaries. Polar does not mean every day is below freezing.
contrast.ru: Полярные круги — астрономические линии широты, а не точные климатические границы. Полярный климат не означает мороз каждый день.

temperate.name: Temperate climates
temperate.rule: Köppen group C generally has milder winters than group D, which has colder continental winters. These groups are defined from temperature and rainfall, not latitude alone: elevation can produce group C climates even within the geographic tropics. Oceans heat and cool more slowly than land, often moderating seasonal temperatures near coasts; winds and currents also matter.
examples: Vancouver, on Canada's Pacific coast, and Winnipeg, deep inside the continent, lie at almost the same latitude. Winnipeg has much colder winters and a larger gap between winter and summer temperatures.

contrast.en: Temperate does not mean mild everywhere: winters in the interior of a continent can be very cold. Classify the climate from its temperatures and rainfall, not from latitude alone.
contrast.ru: Умеренный не значит мягкий везде: зимы в глубине материка могут быть очень холодными. Определяй климат по температуре и осадкам, а не только по широте.

arid.name: Arid climate
arid.rule: Dry climates (Köppen group B) have low precipitation relative to atmospheric water demand; their classification uses rainfall, temperature and rainfall seasonality. Dryness has several causes, including descending subtropical air, distance from oceanic moisture and mountain rain shadows. Group B includes both hot and cold deserts and steppes, so dryness is not defined by heat alone.
examples: The Gobi Desert in Mongolia receives very little rain, but its winters are much colder than in the Sahara.

contrast.en: Arid does not mean hot or completely rainless: it describes a shortage of water.
contrast.ru: Аридный не значит жаркий или совсем без дождей: это нехватка влаги.

sources.section: Köppen groups A–E and highland climates

tropical.name: Tropical climates
tropical.rule: Tropical climates (group A in the Köppen system) are warm in every month, because the Sun stands high near the equator and each square metre receives a lot of solar energy. Rainfall separates the types: rainforest climates have rain in every month, monsoon climates have very heavy rain in one part of the year, and savanna climates have a clear dry season.
examples: Compare a tropical rainforest climate, with substantial rainfall in every month, with a tropical savanna climate, which has a marked dry season. A large river basin can contain more than one rainfall regime.

contrast.en: The geographic tropics, the belt between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, also contain deserts and cool high mountains. Tropical climate (A) is a narrower Köppen type.
contrast.ru: Тропический пояс (широтная зона между тропиками) включает и пустыни, и холодные высокогорья. Тропический климат по Кёппену (A) — более узкое понятие.

sources.title: NOAA JetStream — Climate zones
sources.section: Köppen groups A–E and highland climates

mediterranean.name: Mediterranean climate
mediterranean.rule: Mediterranean climate (group C in the Köppen system) has hot or warm, dry summers and mild, wetter winters. In summer, the subtropical high-pressure belt keeps the air dry; in winter, the belt moves towards the equator and westerly low-pressure systems bring rain. This climate is found on the west coasts of continents: around the Mediterranean Sea, and in parts of California, central Chile and South Africa.
examples: Athens has hot, almost rainless summers, and most of its rain falls between autumn and spring.

contrast.en: Mediterranean names a type of climate, not a place: the type depends on rain and temperature, so it occurs far from the Mediterranean Sea.
contrast.ru: Средиземноморский — название типа климата, а не места: тип определяется осадками и температурой, поэтому он встречается далеко от Средиземного моря.

sources.title: NOAA JetStream — Climate zones
sources.section: Köppen groups A–E and highland climates

mountainous.name: Mountain / highland climates
mountainous.rule: Mountain (highland) climates depend on altitude, the shape of the relief and the side of a mountain that faces the wind. Air gets colder as you climb, so a mountain can be much cooler than lowlands at the same latitude. Moist air forced up a windward slope cools and drops its rain, so the leeward side is often much drier (a rain shadow).
examples: Quito, the capital of Ecuador, lies almost on the equator, but its height in the Andes gives it a cool, mild climate, unlike the hot coastal lowlands.

contrast.en: Temperature usually falls with height, but not always: on calm, clear nights cold air can collect in valleys, so a hilltop can be warmer than the valley floor (a temperature inversion).
contrast.ru: Температура обычно падает с высотой, но не всегда. В тихие ясные ночи холодный воздух стекает и собирается в долинах, поэтому вершина холма может быть теплее дна долины (температурная инверсия).

latitudeSun.title: Latitude and the angle of the Sun's rays
latitudeSun.description: The equator receives more solar heat than the poles. The main cause is the angle at which the rays strike the surface, which controls insolation (the solar energy received per square metre).

physics.name: Solar angle and latitude
physics.rule: A beam that strikes the ground straight on covers a small area, so each square metre gets a lot of energy. At a lower angle, the same beam spreads over a larger area, so each square metre gets less energy. On average over a year, high latitudes therefore receive less solar energy per square metre than low latitudes.
examples: Shine a torch straight down onto a sheet of paper, then at a shallow angle. The bright patch becomes longer and dimmer.

review.russianTerm: Угол падения солнечных лучей и широта

contrast.en: The Sun's height in the sky changes with latitude, season and time of day: even on the equator, the Sun is overhead at noon only at the equinoxes.
contrast.ru: Высота Солнца над горизонтом меняется с широтой, сезоном и временем суток: даже на экваторе Солнце бывает в зените в полдень только в дни равноденствий.

tilt.name: Axial tilt and seasons
tilt.rule: Earth's axis is tilted relative to the perpendicular to its orbital plane. As a result, each hemisphere leans towards the Sun for part of the year and away from it for the rest. This changes the length of day and the height of the Sun at noon, so the two hemispheres have opposite seasons.
examples: In June, Moscow has long days and a high midday Sun, while Sydney, in the Southern Hemisphere, is in winter.

review.russianTerm: Наклон земной оси и времена года

contrast.en: Seasons come mainly from the tilt, not from changing distance: Earth is closest to the Sun during the Northern Hemisphere's winter.
contrast.ru: Смену сезонов вызывает прежде всего наклон оси, а не изменение расстояния до Солнца: Земля ближе всего к Солнцу зимой в Северном полушарии.

circulation.title: Atmospheric circulation cells
circulation.items: Air rises near the equator and sinks in the subtropics. In each hemisphere this pattern is made up of three idealised cells: Hadley, Ferrel and polar. The Coriolis effect, caused by Earth’s rotation, deflects winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern. Together with the cells, it creates wind belts (trade winds, westerlies and polar easterlies). The cells also create pressure belts: low pressure near the equator and in subpolar latitudes, high pressure in the subtropics and at the poles.

hadley.name: Hadley cell
hadley.rule: The Hadley cell is the tropical loop of air. Air is heated near the equator, rises and flows towards the poles high up. It cools and sinks around the subtropics, then flows back towards the equator near the surface. The Coriolis effect turns this surface flow into the north-east and south-east trade winds.
examples: The Sahara lies in the subtropical belt of sinking air, which is one reason it is so dry.

contrast.en: The three-cell model is an average over long periods and over all longitudes. Real zones of rising and sinking air are not fixed at one latitude. They move with the seasons.
contrast.ru: Модель трёх ячеек — усреднённая картина за длительный период и по всей долготе. Реальные зоны подъёма и опускания воздуха не привязаны к одной широте: они смещаются вместе с сезонами.

sources.title: Met Office — Global circulation patterns
sources.section: Hadley cell; Ferrel cell; Polar cell; Coriolis effect

ferrel.name: Ferrel cell
ferrel.rule: The Ferrel cell is the circulation in mid-latitudes, between the subtropical and polar cells. Surface air moves towards the poles, and air higher up moves back towards the equator. It is not driven directly by heating. Mid-latitude weather systems, such as depressions and anticyclones, keep it going by moving heat and momentum.
examples: In the UK, the prevailing wind comes from the south-west, so weather systems usually arrive from the Atlantic.

contrast.en: Prevailing westerlies are only an average. On a given day, mid-latitude winds can blow from many directions as depressions and anticyclones pass.
contrast.ru: Преобладающие западные ветры — это только среднее. В конкретный день ветер умеренных широт может дуть с разных сторон, когда над территорией проходят циклоны и антициклоны.

sources.title: Met Office — Global circulation patterns
sources.section: Hadley cell; Ferrel cell; Polar cell; Coriolis effect

polar.name: Polar cell
polar.rule: Over the poles, cold, dense air sinks and creates high pressure. At the surface it flows towards lower latitudes, where it meets the warmer air of the mid-latitudes at the polar front. There the air rises and returns towards the poles higher up.
examples: In winter, cold air from the polar regions can spread south and bring severe frost to northern Canada and Siberia.

contrast.en: A wind is named after the direction it blows from. Polar easterlies blow from the east, and westerlies blow from the west.
contrast.ru: Ветер называют по направлению, откуда он дует. Полярные восточные ветры дуют с востока, а западные — с запада.

sources.title: Met Office — Global circulation patterns
sources.section: Hadley cell; Ferrel cell; Polar cell; Coriolis effect

pressure.title: High & low pressure
pressure.high: A high-pressure area usually brings settled, dry weather. Wind blows from high to low pressure, so air flows outwards from the centre of the high.
pressure.low: As air rises over a low, it cools and its water vapour condenses, forming cloud. Rain is likely when the air is moist, so low pressure usually brings unsettled weather.

high.name: High-pressure system (anticyclone)
high.rule: A high-pressure system (anticyclone) is an area where surface air pressure is higher than in its surroundings. Air sinks over it, is compressed and warms, so its relative humidity falls and clouds struggle to form.
examples: A clear anticyclonic winter night can cool strongly by radiation.

contrast.en: High pressure does not always mean warm or clear weather: in winter, fog and low cloud can persist under a high. Wind strength depends on how quickly pressure changes over a distance, not on whether the system is high or low.
contrast.ru: Высокое давление не всегда означает тепло и ясное небо: зимой под антициклоном могут держаться туман и низкая облачность. Сила ветра зависит от того, насколько быстро давление меняется на расстоянии, а не от того, высокое оно или низкое.

sources.title: Met Office — High and low pressure
sources.section: Characteristics of high and low pressure; wind flow and pressure

low.name: Low-pressure system (cyclone / depression)
low.rule: A low-pressure system is an area where surface air pressure is lower than in its surroundings. Air is drawn in at the surface and converges, so it has to rise.
examples: On a weather map, isobars are lines joining places of equal pressure. Where they are close together, pressure changes quickly over a short distance, and the wind is usually strong.

contrast.en: Mid-latitude lows (depressions) and tropical cyclones can both be called cyclones, but they are different systems. Mid-latitude lows often have fronts; tropical cyclones have a warm core.
contrast.ru: Внетропические циклоны (depressions) и тропические циклоны можно назвать одним словом «циклон», но это разные системы. У внетропических циклонов часто есть фронты, а у тропических — тёплое ядро.

sources.section: Characteristics of high and low pressure; wind flow and pressure

tropicalStorms.title: Tropical storms
tropicalStorms.description: A tropical cyclone is an organised, rotating low-pressure system with a warm core. It forms over tropical or subtropical oceans.

formation.name: Tropical cyclone formation
formation.rule: Warm seawater supplies moisture to the air. In an existing cluster of storms, moist air rises and cools; water vapour condenses and releases latent heat. This helps sustain rising air and the developing low-pressure circulation. Air flows inward near the surface and is deflected by Earth’s rotation. Weak vertical wind shear helps the storm’s circulation remain organised.
examples: Many typhoons in the western Pacific form in late summer and early autumn, when the sea has been warm for weeks.

contrast.en: Warm water is necessary but not enough on its own: the air must also be moist and unstable, and the wind must not change much with height. Cyclones also rarely form right on the equator, where the Coriolis effect is almost zero.
contrast.ru: Одной тёплой воды недостаточно: нужны ещё влажный неустойчивый воздух и слабый сдвиг ветра по высоте. Циклоны почти не возникают прямо на экваторе, где эффект Кориолиса почти равен нулю.

naming.name: Hurricane, typhoon and tropical cyclone
naming.rule: Hurricane and typhoon are regional names for sufficiently strong tropical cyclones: hurricane in the Atlantic and northeast/central Pacific, typhoon in the northwest Pacific. Other basins use their own cyclone classifications.
examples: A storm with a low wind category can still flood a low-lying coastal town if its storm surge arrives at high tide.

contrast.en: The Saffir–Simpson scale rates only sustained hurricane wind, not rainfall or storm surge. Other basins use different scales or classifications.
contrast.ru: Шкала Саффира–Симпсона (Saffir–Simpson scale) оценивает только устойчивый ветер урагана, а не дождь и нагон. В других районах мира используют свои шкалы и классификации.

impacts.name: How tropical cyclones cause damage
impacts.rule: Strong winds, large waves and storm surge damage buildings and flood low-lying coasts. Heavy rain causes inland flooding and can trigger landslides on steep slopes. Losses depend on exposure (how many people and assets are in the path) and vulnerability (how easily they can be harmed). The early warning people receive and their ability to respond also matter.
examples: When an early warning is issued in time, families can move to a shelter on high ground before the surge arrives. Stronger building codes mean roofs and walls are less likely to fail in strong winds.

review.russianTerm: Опасные процессы и последствия тропического циклона

contrast.en: Storm surge is an abnormal rise above the predicted tide, not simply one large breaking wave. State the initiating event when separating primary from secondary effects.
contrast.ru: Штормовой нагон — аномальное повышение уровня относительно ожидаемого прилива, а не просто одна большая волна. При делении на первичные и вторичные последствия укажи исходное событие.

enso.title: El Niño / La Niña / ENSO-neutral
enso.normal: ENSO (El Niño–Southern Oscillation) is a natural climate pattern in the equatorial Pacific. Its neutral phase is the usual state, when neither El Niño nor La Niña conditions dominate.
enso.elNino: El Niño is the warm phase of ENSO: the surface of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific becomes unusually warm. It is linked to weaker trade winds and to shifts in weather across many parts of the world.
enso.laNina: La Niña is the cool phase of ENSO: the surface of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific becomes unusually cold. It often comes with stronger trade winds.

normal.name: ENSO-neutral Pacific conditions
normal.rule: Trade winds blow from east to west along the equator. They push warm surface water towards Indonesia and Australia, so the water there is warmer and the sea level is higher. Surface water is pulled away from the coast of South America, and cold water rises from below to replace it. This upwelling, the rise of cold deep water, brings nutrients to the surface.
examples: Off the coast of Peru, upwelling brings nutrient-rich water to the surface, which supports a large fishery.

review.russianTerm: Нейтральные условия ЭНЮК в Тихом океане

contrast.en: Neutral does not mean no weather extremes or no variability; ENSO is only one influence on climate.
contrast.ru: Нейтральная фаза не означает отсутствия экстремальной погоды или изменчивости: ЭНЮК — лишь один из факторов климата.

elNino.name: El Niño
elNino.rule: Trade winds weaken, so less warm water is pushed west and warm water drifts back east. The central and eastern Pacific become unusually warm, and upwelling off South America weakens because less cold water reaches the surface. Warm, moist air now rises over the central Pacific instead of the west, so rainfall shifts eastwards.
examples: Off Peru, a strong El Niño weakens upwelling, so fewer nutrients reach the surface and the fish catch often falls.

contrast.en: El Niño changes the odds of regional weather; it does not guarantee a fixed list of floods or droughts. Events recur irregularly, every few years.
contrast.ru: Эль-Ниньо меняет вероятность региональной погоды, но не гарантирует определённого набора наводнений и засух. События повторяются нерегулярно, примерно каждые несколько лет.

laNina.name: La Niña
laNina.rule: The trade winds strengthen and push more warm water west. Upwelling off South America increases, so more cold water rises and the eastern Pacific becomes cooler than normal. Rain and storm clouds gather over the western Pacific, while the central and eastern Pacific become drier.
examples: In eastern Australia, La Niña years often bring heavier rain, which can increase the risk of flooding.

contrast.en: Regional impacts are not exact mirror images of every El Niño event; an ENSO phase alone is not a local forecast.
contrast.ru: Последствия Ла-Нинья в регионах не всегда противоположны последствиям Эль-Ниньо. Сама фаза ЭНЮК не даёт местного прогноза погоды.

haiyan.title: Case study — Typhoon Haiyan (Nov 2013)
haiyan.scale: A very powerful tropical cyclone with destructive winds and coastal storm-surge flooding. Surge depth varied by location; a single value does not describe the whole coast.

seep.social: Social: a GIZ assessment from May 2014 reports more than 6,000 deaths and about 4 million displaced people. Displaced people had to leave their homes. Affected people, who suffered any kind of harm, are a different measure.
seep.economic: Economic: homes, businesses and transport infrastructure were damaged; losses depend on which assets and reporting period are counted.
seep.environmental: Environmental: storm surge flooded coastal land, while strong winds damaged vegetation and spread debris.
seep.political: Political: the response depended on local government capacity.

responses.local: Local: residents and responders carried out evacuation and rescue under severe disruption.
responses.government: Government: storm warnings and evacuation orders were issued, but some evacuation centres were themselves exposed to storm surge. The assessment identified gaps between hazard forecasts and local warnings.
responses.shortTerm: Short term: emergency relief addressed shelter, food, safe water and medical needs.
responses.longTerm: Long term: the GIZ assessment recommended clearer warnings, better hazard maps and safer evacuation centres. These are recommendations, not proof that they were carried out.

bigDry.title: Case study — Australia’s Millennium Drought
bigDry.summary: Drought is a long period of much less rain than normal, so water supplies, soil moisture and river flows fall below what people, farming and ecosystems need. A long drought, known as the Millennium Drought, affected south-eastern Australia from about 1997 to 2009. Low rainfall and over-allocation of water cut river flows and threatened water supplies. The crisis was worst in the later years of the drought, when river flows and lake levels were at their lowest.

seep.social: Social: the water supply to Adelaide and to towns around the Lower Lakes was at risk, and households faced water restrictions.
seep.economic: Economic: water for irrigation was cut sharply, which hurt farming and horticulture.
seep.environmental: Environmental: low lake levels exposed acid sulfate soils; salinity increased and wetlands lost connectivity.
seep.political: Political: the drought showed weaknesses in water management.

responses.government: Government: basin-wide planning, water returned to rivers and wetlands for the environment, and changes in how water is shared.

climateChange.title: Climate change over time
climateChange.evidence:
Ice cores, tree rings and atmospheric measurements show how the climate has changed. Natural factors have changed it in the past.

- Milankovitch cycles: changes in Earth’s orbit and tilt alter how sunlight is spread across latitudes and seasons. These cycles last about 100,000 years (eccentricity), 41,000 years (axial tilt) and 23,000 years (precession); the figures are rounded (FAU data).
- Sunspots: the number of sunspots rises and falls in a cycle of about 11 years (NASA data). Solar activity is a weak factor: its cycle changes the Sun’s energy output only slightly, so its effect on temperature is small.
- Large explosive eruptions can inject sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, where reactions form sulfate aerosols that reflect sunlight. After the eruption of Mount Pinatubo in 1991, global temperatures fell for a short time.

Natural variability still affects individual years and regions. However, natural forcing alone cannot explain the observed recent long-term global warming; its main driver is human greenhouse gas emissions, especially from burning fossil fuels.
climateChange.mitigation: Mitigation means cutting greenhouse gas emissions or removing gases from the atmosphere, so that climate change is slower and weaker. Examples: renewable energy such as wind and solar power, carbon capture and storage, and reforestation.
climateChange.adaptation: Adaptation means adjusting to the effects of climate change that are already happening or expected, so that people and ecosystems are less harmed. Examples: sea walls against rising sea levels, drought-resistant crops and early warning systems for floods and storms.
